cards.text: Welcome to the church at Antioch, friend! It's got a whole team of prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen and Saul. Five names on the roster, and one of them grew up with somebody you would NOT expect.

cards.question: Manaen, one of the teachers at Antioch, was brought up with somebody famous. Who?

cards.text: While they're worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit speaks, and He says to set apart two of these five for the work He's called them to. I bet those two felt like you do when the boss says your name in a meeting, friend, times a THOUSAND.

cards.question: The Holy Spirit says to set apart two of the five prophets and teachers at Antioch. Which two?
After they fast and pray, they lay their ___ on Barnabas and Saul and send them off.

cards.text: Sent out by the Holy Spirit, Barnabas and Saul go down to Seleucia and set sail. When the Holy Spirit is the one sending you, friend, you do NOT argue about the window seat.

cards.question: From Seleucia, Barnabas and Saul sail to the island of ___.

cards.text: They land at Salamis and start proclaiming the word of God. Me? I can't even find my apron for the first ten minutes of a shift.

cards.question: In Salamis, Barnabas and Saul proclaim the word of God in the Jewish ___.
John, also called Mark, goes to Cyprus with Barnabas and Saul. What is his role on the trip?

cards.text: They travel the whole island as far as Paphos, and there they find a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus. Sorcerer AND false prophet, friend, that's two titles on one business card, and neither one is good news.

cards.question: Bar-Jesus is an attendant of the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a man of intelligence. Why does the proconsul call for Barnabas and Saul?

answers.text: He wants to hear the word of God
He wants them off his island
He wants them put under arrest

cards.question: Bar-Jesus, also called Elymas the sorcerer, backs up Barnabas and Saul in front of the proconsul.

cards.text: Nope, Elymas opposes them and tries to turn the proconsul from the faith. Then Saul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looks right at him, and it's the kind of look that makes a grown man put his phone DOWN.

cards.question: Saul goes by another name too. He's also called ___.

cards.text: Paul doesn't hold back, calling Elymas a “child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness” who's full of deceit and trickery. I've had an oven timer yell at me for ten straight minutes, and it NEVER got that specific.

cards.question: Paul tells Elymas the hand of the Lord is against him. What does Paul say will happen to Elymas?

answers.text: He will be blind for a time
He will lose his voice for a time
He will be driven out of Paphos

cards.text: Immediately, mist and darkness come over Elymas. He gropes around, looking for someone to lead him by the hand.

cards.question: After the proconsul Sergius Paulus sees what happened to Elymas, he sends Barnabas and Saul away.

cards.text: Sergius Paulus believes, astonished at the teaching about the Lord. Hold that thought, friend, because Barnabas and Paul have a LOT more road in front of them.

findings.problem: The joke blends the everyday comparison into the Bible scene. It puts an airplane 'window seat' onto Barnabas and Saul's actual ship from Seleucia. The comparison and the Bible setting become one mixed image instead of two separate ones.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The question calls him 'John, also called Mark.' Acts 13:5 says only 'John.' The 'Mark' detail comes from outside the passage (Acts 12:12, 25) and has no reference. The card can't carry one, because a choice card cites only the verses of its right answer (Acts 13:5). Drop 'also called Mark' or move the outside fact to a story card that cites it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The statement 'he sends Barnabas and Saul away' is marked False, but Acts 13:12 never says whether the proconsul sends them away. It only says he believed. The text never shows the statement is false, so a baker could argue it either way. Ask about what the verse does say, such as whether he believes.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
